n: With a church established in Ishmael, Lamoni wants to take Ammon to the land of Nephi to meet his father, the high king.
The Lord warns Ammon not to go — the high king would try to kill him — and sends him instead to Middoni, where his brother Aaron and companions Muloki and Ammah are imprisoned.

f.g: Two of the missionaries who came with the sons of Mosiah.

n: Ammon tells Lamoni he is going to free his brothers in Middoni.

f.w: I go that I may deliver them

n: Lamoni, believing Ammon can do all things in the Lord’s strength, offers to go too, since Middoni’s king Antiomno is his friend. He asks how Ammon learned of the imprisonment.

f.w: in the strength of the Lord thou canst do all things

f.g: King over the land of Middoni.

n: No one told him but God.
Lamoni has his servants ready the horses and chariots.
Lamoni pledges to plead with Middoni’s king for the prisoners’ release.

f.g: Lamoni uses his royal friendships to help.

n: On the road they meet Lamoni’s father, the high king over all the land.
The father demands to know why Lamoni missed his great feast.
He also wants to know why Lamoni is traveling with a Nephite, “one of the children of a liar” — echoing an old Lamanite grudge against Nephi.
Lamoni, afraid of offending his father, explains where he is going.

f.g: Lamoni is a vassal king answering to his father.

n: He also explains why he missed the feast — his conversion.
To Lamoni’s surprise, his father is furious, repeating the old charge that Nephi robbed their ancestors and that Nephites come only to deceive and rob them again.

f.g: Refers to the brass plates and Nephi’s leadership, long resented by the Lamanites.

n: The father orders Lamoni to kill Ammon and return to Ishmael.
Lamoni refuses: he will not kill Ammon or turn back, for Ammon’s brothers are just men and holy prophets.

f.g: A new convert courageously defying a powerful father.

n: Enraged, his father draws his sword to kill his own son.

f.g: The hatred of tradition runs so deep that the king would kill his own son.

n: Ammon steps in: don’t kill your son. He has repented and would be saved — but if you die now, in anger, your soul is lost.

f.w: thy soul could not be saved

n: Killing an innocent son would make his blood cry to God for vengeance.

f.w: his blood would cry from the ground

n: The king blames Ammon: killing my son would be shedding innocent blood, but it is you who are trying to destroy him.

f.w: it is thou that hast sought to destroy him
f.g: He blames Ammon for turning his son against him.

n: He attacks Ammon, who blocks his blows and wounds his arm so he can’t use it.
Realizing Ammon could kill him, the king begs for his life.

f.g: The powerful king now pleads with the servant.

n: Ammon raises his sword and demands the release of his brothers as the price of the king’s life.

f.g: Ammon uses the moment to free the prisoners, not to kill.

n: The terrified king offers anything — even half his kingdom.

f.w: even to half of the kingdom

n: Ammon asks only for his brothers’ release and for Lamoni to keep his kingdom and his freedom without his father’s displeasure.

f.w: that Lamoni may retain his kingdom
f.g: Ammon thinks of his friend before himself.

n: The king rejoices that his life is spared.
Astonished that Ammon wants nothing for himself and loves Lamoni so much, the king grants Lamoni independence forever.

f.w: the great love he had for his son Lamoni
f.g: Ammon’s unselfish love softens the old king’s heart.

n: He also frees the prisoners and invites Ammon and his brothers to visit him, eager to learn what they and Lamoni teach.

f.w: he was desirous to learn them

n: Ammon and Lamoni reach Middoni, Lamoni wins the king’s favor, and the prisoners are released.

f.w: found favor in the eyes of the king
f.g: Lamoni’s friendship with Antiomno pays off.

n: Ammon grieves to see them naked, their skin worn raw by cords, having suffered hunger, thirst, and much else — yet they had been patient throughout.
Their lot was a harder people. They had been rejected, beaten, chased from place to place, and finally imprisoned in Middoni until Lamoni and Ammon freed them.

f.w: more hardened and a more stiffnecked people
